title: The Secret Life of Word Roots

sentences.en: If you could see through the cover of an English dictionary, you would notice something surprising.
sentences.zh: 如果你能透过英语词典的封面看进去，你会注意到一件奇怪的事。

sentences.en: English words are not strangers to each other.
sentences.zh: 英语单词之间并非毫不相干的陌生人。

sentences.en: Thousands of them belong to a small number of families, like cousins who share the same grandfather.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的词属于少数几个家族，就像共有一位祖父的堂表兄弟姐妹。

sentences.en: The head of each family is not a word at all, but a root: a short piece of ancient Latin that carries one basic meaning.
sentences.zh: 每个家族的族长根本不是一个词，而是一个词根：一小段承载着单一基本含义的古老拉丁文。

sentences.en: Consider the root spect, which comes from the Latin word meaning "to look".
sentences.zh: 以词根 spect 为例，它来自拉丁语，意思是"看"。

sentences.en: Add different beginnings and endings, and a whole family of words appears.
sentences.zh: 加上不同的前缀和后缀，整整一个单词家族便浮现出来。

sentences.en: When you inspect something, you look into it closely.
sentences.zh: 当你 inspect（检查）某物时，你是往里仔细地看。

sentences.en: A spectator is a person who looks at a game or a show.
sentences.zh: spectator（观众）就是观看比赛或演出的人。

sentences.en: When you respect someone, you look up to them, again and again.
sentences.zh: 当你 respect（尊敬）某人时，你是一再地抬头仰望他们。

sentences.en: In retrospect means looking back at the past.
sentences.zh: in retrospect 意为回顾过去。

sentences.en: And a prospect is a possible future that you look forward to.
sentences.zh: 而 prospect（前景）是你向前眺望的那个可能的未来。

sentences.en: One root, ten doors.
sentences.zh: 一个词根，十扇门。

sentences.en: Learn one key, and a whole corridor opens.
sentences.zh: 掌握一把钥匙，整条走廊便向你敞开。

sentences.en: Now look at struct, which means "to build".
sentences.zh: 再看 struct，它的意思是"建造"。

sentences.en: To construct a bridge is to build it, piece by piece.
sentences.zh: construct（建造）一座桥，就是把它一块一块地建起来。

sentences.en: A structure is anything that has been built, from a bird's nest to a skyscraper.
sentences.zh: structure（结构、建筑物）指任何被建造出来的东西，从鸟窝到摩天大楼。

sentences.en: To instruct a student is, in a beautiful sense, to build knowledge inside them.
sentences.zh: instruct（教导）一个学生，从某种美妙的意义上说，是在他心里建造知识。

sentences.en: And destroy simply means to un-build something: the Latin prefix de- takes the building apart.
sentences.zh: 而 destroy（摧毁）的意思就是"拆掉"：拉丁前缀 de- 把建筑物拆散。

sentences.en: Port means "to carry".
sentences.zh: port 的意思是"携带、搬运"。

sentences.en: It hides inside transport (to carry across), import (to carry into a country), and export (to carry out).
sentences.zh: 它藏在 transport（运输，横着搬）、import（进口，搬进来）和 export（出口，搬出去）里面。

sentences.en: A portable radio is light enough to be carried by one hand.
sentences.zh: portable 收音机轻到一只手就能拎走。

sentences.en: A porter is a person whose whole job is to carry travelers' bags.
sentences.zh: porter（搬运工）就是以替旅客搬行李为业的人。

sentences.en: Even the word report contains this root: a report carries information back to someone.
sentences.zh: 连 report 这个词里也藏着它：report（报告）就是把信息搬回去交给别人。

sentences.en: And opportunity? Sailors once used it for a favorable wind that carried a ship safely toward port.
sentences.zh: 那 opportunity 呢？水手们曾用它指那阵把船稳稳送向港口的顺风。

sentences.en: The root ject means "to throw".
sentences.zh: 词根 ject 的意思是"扔、投掷"。

sentences.en: To reject a plan is to throw it back.
sentences.zh: reject（拒绝）一个计划，就是把它扔回去。

sentences.en: To eject something is to throw it out.
sentences.zh: eject（弹出、驱逐）就是把它扔出去。

sentences.en: To inject medicine is to throw it into the body through a needle.
sentences.zh: inject（注射）就是通过针头把药液掷入体内。

sentences.en: And when you object to an idea, you throw your own opinion in its way.
sentences.zh: 而当你 object（反对）一个观点时，你是把自己的意见拦在了它的去路上。

sentences.en: A project, such as a school science project, is literally a plan thrown forward into the future.
sentences.zh: project（项目，如学校的科学项目），字面意思就是投向未来的一份计划。

sentences.en: What is truly amazing is where these roots come from.
sentences.zh: 更令人惊叹的是这些词根的来历。

sentences.en: More than two thousand years ago, Roman soldiers, merchants, and teachers spread Latin across Europe.
sentences.zh: 两千多年前，罗马的士兵、商人和教师把拉丁语传遍了欧洲。

sentences.en: After the Roman Empire fell, Latin did not die; it simply changed its clothes.
sentences.zh: 罗马帝国衰亡后，拉丁语并没有死，它只是换了一身衣裳。

sentences.en: It transformed slowly into French, Italian, Spanish, and the other Romance languages.
sentences.zh: 它慢慢 transformed（转变）为法语、意大利语、西班牙语等罗曼语族语言。

sentences.en: In 1066, French-speaking rulers arrived in England, and their vocabulary was imported into English like goods into a harbor.
sentences.zh: 1066年，讲法语的统治者来到英格兰，他们的词汇像进港的货物一样被 imported（引入）英语。

sentences.en: That is why English often has two words for one idea: a plain one like "begin" beside a Latin-flavored one like "commence".
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么英语常为一个意思备两个词：朴素的 begin，与带着拉丁味的 commence。

sentences.en: Roots are not only Latin, of course; Greek also donated generously.
sentences.zh: 词根当然不只来自拉丁语，希腊语也十分慷慨。

sentences.en: Bio means "life", so biology is the study of living things.
sentences.zh: bio 意为"生命"，所以 biology 是研究生物的学问。

sentences.en: Graph means "to write", so a photograph is "light writing" and a biography is "life writing".
sentences.zh: graph 意为"写"，所以 photograph 是"光的书写"，biography 是"人生的书写"。

sentences.en: Phon means "sound": a telephone carries "far sound", and a symphony puts "sounds together".
sentences.zh: phon 意为"声音"：telephone 传送"远方的声音"，symphony 则把"声音放在一起"。

sentences.en: Once you begin to notice roots, you see them everywhere, like a hidden pattern printed under the surface of the language.
sentences.zh: 一旦你开始留意词根，你会发现它们无处不在，像印在语言表层之下的一幅隐藏图案。

sentences.en: Even scientists use the trick: when doctors invent a new medical term, they usually construct it from these same roots, like bricks.
sentences.zh: 连科学家都用这一招：医生发明新医学术语时，通常也用这些词根像砌砖一样 construct 出来。

sentences.en: For a Chinese student, this is very good news.
sentences.zh: 对中国学生来说，这是个天大的好消息。

sentences.en: You do not need to memorize ten thousand words one by one.
sentences.zh: 你不必一个一个地死记一万个单词。

sentences.en: You need perhaps two hundred roots, and then many new words will introduce themselves to you, already half familiar.
sentences.zh: 你也许只需两百个词根，然后许多生词便会主动向你自我介绍——你已经对它们眼熟了。

sentences.en: Of course, roots cannot predict every meaning; languages are full of surprises and stubborn exceptions.
sentences.zh: 当然，词根不能 predict（预测）每个词义；语言里满是意外和固执的例外。

sentences.en: But they can always offer a reliable first guess, and confidence is half the battle in reading.
sentences.zh: 但它们总能给出靠谱的第一猜测，而信心正是阅读这场战役的一半胜算。

sentences.en: So the next time you meet a long, frightening English word, do not panic.
sentences.zh: 所以下次遇到一个又长又吓人的英语单词时，别慌。

sentences.en: Inspect it calmly, look for a familiar root in the middle, and let the word tell you its own history.
sentences.zh: 冷静地 inspect（审视）它，在词中寻找那个熟悉的词根，让这个词亲口讲出自己的历史。

sentences.en: In retrospect, you may wonder why English ever looked so difficult.
sentences.zh: 回头看（in retrospect），你也许会奇怪：英语当初怎么会显得那么难。

questions.explain: "the root spect, which comes from the Latin word meaning 'to look'" —— spect = 看。

questions.q: The word "report" contains the root "port". What does this tell us about its original meaning?
options: It carries information back to someone.
questions.explain: "a report carries information back to someone" —— 报告就是把信息"搬"回去。

questions.q: Why does English often have two words for one idea, like "begin" and "commence"?
options: French-speaking rulers brought many Latin-based words to England in 1066.
questions.explain: 1066年法语统治者的词汇"像进港货物一样"融入英语，形成本族词与拉丁味词并存的格局。

questions.q: What does the root "graph" mean in words like photograph and biography?
questions.explain: "Graph means 'to write'" —— photograph 是"光的书写"，biography 是"人生的书写"。

questions.q: According to the passage, how do word roots help learners most?
options: They give a reliable first guess at new words' meanings.
They explain the history of Chinese characters.
questions.explain: 结尾：词根虽不能 predict 每个词义，但总能给出"reliable first guess"，信心是阅读制胜的一半。
